Baume & Mercier.name: Riviera
Baume & Mercier.desc: A 1970s-style sports watch with a twelve-sided bezel and integrated bracelet, now with the long-running Baumatic movement.

Baume & Mercier.name: Clifton
Baume & Mercier.desc: A classic round dress watch with vintage lines, offered with Baume's five-day Baumatic movement at a fair price.

Baume & Mercier.name: Classima
Baume & Mercier.desc: The brand's entry-level dress watch, a simple and slim round design for everyday office wear.

Baume & Mercier.name: Hampton
Baume & Mercier.desc: A rectangular Art Deco style watch, the brand's main shaped case for people who want something other than round.

Fortis.name: Marinemaster
Fortis.desc: A tough everyday sports watch with a 60-minute bezel, bold colours and 200m water resistance.

Fortis.name: Flieger
Fortis.desc: A clean, highly legible pilot watch from a brand with decades of real aviation and space history.

Fortis.name: Stratoliner
Fortis.desc: A sporty chronograph with colourful textured dials inspired by space flights, Fortis's flagship stopwatch.

Formex.name: Essence
Formex.desc: An everyday sports watch with a shock-absorbing case and a clever adjustable bracelet, sold in ThirtyNine, FortyOne and FortyThree sizes.

Formex.name: Reef
Formex.desc: A 300m dive watch with a certified accurate movement and quick-change bracelet, strong value for a Swiss diver.

Formex.name: Field Automatic
Formex.desc: A light titanium field watch under $1,000, simple to read and built for outdoor use.

Nomos.name: Tangente
Nomos.desc: The Bauhaus-style watch that made Nomos famous, very thin with a clean dial and in-house German movement.

Nomos.name: Club Campus
Nomos.desc: A casual, sporty-looking watch with a playful dial, the cheapest way into a German in-house movement.

Nomos.name: Club Sport neomatik
Nomos.desc: A thin steel sports watch on a bracelet, a lighter and more modern alternative to bigger sports watches.

Nomos.name: Orion
Nomos.desc: An elegant dress watch with a domed dial and fine stick markers, more formal than the Tangente.

Nomos.name: Metro
Nomos.desc: A modern design with a distinctive seconds dial and coloured accents, using Nomos's own escapement.

Sinn.desc: A simple, tough everyday watch from a German tool-watch maker, one of the best values in Sinn's range.
A pilot-style watch with a rotating bezel and day-date, rugged and easy to read.
Sinn's classic pilot chronograph with a rotating bezel, a design little changed in decades.
A pilot watch with a scratch-hardened steel case and magnetic shielding, also offered with a second time zone.

Sinn.name: U1
Sinn.desc: A big dive watch made from German submarine steel, built to survive extreme depth and pressure.

Sinn.name: EZM
Sinn.desc: Sinn's mission-timer tool watches made for police and rescue units, the toughest pieces in the range.

Damasko.name: DK
Damasko.desc: Everyday sports watches with Damasko's very hard, scratch-resistant steel, including the popular DK47.

Damasko.name: DA
Damasko.desc: Damasko's classic pilot watches with hardened cases and simple, legible dials.

Damasko.name: DS
Damasko.desc: The brand's affordable three-hand watch, a no-fuss field design in hardened steel.

Damasko.name: DC
Damasko.movement: Automatic chronograph, Valjoux 7750 or in-house C51
Damasko.desc: Tough pilot-style chronographs, some with Damasko's own movement, built for heavy daily wear.

Tutima.name: M2 Seven Seas
Tutima.desc: A light titanium dive watch with 500m water resistance, Tutima's best value model.

Tutima.name: M2
Tutima.desc: A large titanium pilot chronograph derived from a watch made for German air force pilots.

Tutima.name: Flieger
Tutima.desc: A classic military-style pilot watch with a big crown and bold numerals.

Tutima.name: Grand Flieger
Tutima.desc: A vintage-inspired pilot chronograph echoing Tutima's 1940s military watches.

Tutima.name: Patria
Tutima.desc: A fine dress watch with a movement made and decorated in Glashutte, Tutima's high-end showpiece.

Hanhart.name: 417 ES
Hanhart.desc: A faithful remake of a 1950s German military pilot chronograph with a two-register dial and red-marked bezel.

Hanhart.name: Primus Pilot
Hanhart.desc: A modern pilot watch with Hanhart's signature red pusher look and a bold, easy-to-read dial.

Hanhart.name: Primus Diver
Hanhart.desc: A sturdy modern dive watch from the Primus family with a sporty, technical design.

Hanhart.name: Primus Racer
Hanhart.desc: A motorsport-themed chronograph with bright accents, the sportiest of the Primus line.

King Seiko.name: KSK
King Seiko.desc: A crisp, sharply faceted remake of the 1965 King Seiko, with a mirror-polished case and dressy feel.

King Seiko.name: KS1969
King Seiko.desc: A cushion-shaped revival of the 1969 King Seiko with a slim movement and finely finished case.

King Seiko.name: VANAC
King Seiko.desc: An angular, colourful 1970s-style sports watch with a Grand Seiko-derived high-beat movement, offered in steel and titanium.

Grand Seiko quartz.name: Heritage 9F
Grand Seiko quartz.desc: Grand Seiko's classic dress design with a high-accuracy quartz movement accurate to about ten seconds a year.

Grand Seiko quartz.name: Sport 9F GMT
Grand Seiko quartz.desc: A travel watch with a second time zone hand, combining Grand Seiko finishing with near-zero maintenance quartz.

The Citizen quartz.name: The Citizen Eco-Drive A060
The Citizen quartz.desc: A titanium dress watch powered by light and accurate to about five seconds a year, Citizen's top quartz watch.

The Citizen quartz.name: The Citizen Caliber 0200
The Citizen quartz.desc: The Citizen's high-end mechanical watch, finished by hand in Switzerland and Japan; not quartz but sold alongside the A060.

Minase.name: Divido
Minase.desc: Minase's only round watch, with a sculpted case that frames the dial and very high hand finishing.

Minase.name: 7 Windows
Minase.desc: A shaped case with seven sapphire windows that show off the movement, the brand's signature design.

Minase.name: 5 Windows
Minase.desc: A tonneau-style case with sapphire side windows, including a smaller Midsize version.

Minase.name: Horizon
Minase.desc: Minase's most accessible model, a compact sports watch with a rubber strap or bracelet option.

Ming.name: 37 series
Ming.desc: Ming's core design with layered sapphire dials and floating markers, including the 37.09 and 37.06.

Ming.name: 17 series
Ming.desc: Ming's affordable steel line, the easiest way into the brand's modern dial style.

Ming.name: 57 series
Ming.desc: Ming's complicated line, including the 57.04 Phoenix monopusher chronograph and 57.05 Comet worldtimer.
Ming's high-end flagship with a bespoke hand-finished movement, made in small series.

Oak & Oscar.name: Humboldt
Oak & Oscar.desc: A Chicago-designed field watch with a sandwich dial and dense lume, the brand's permanent core model.

Oak & Oscar.name: Humboldt GMT
Oak & Oscar.desc: The Humboldt with a second time zone hand, a rugged travel watch from a small American brand.

Oak & Oscar.name: Olmsted
Oak & Oscar.desc: A smaller, simpler field watch that is one of the best-value American-designed Swiss watches.

Oak & Oscar.name: Atwood
Oak & Oscar.desc: A vintage racing-style chronograph with a hand-wound flyback movement, Oak & Oscar's newest stopwatch.

Lorca.name: Model No.1 GMT
Lorca.desc: A compact retro-styled travel watch with a true GMT movement, praised as strong value from a US brand.

Lorca.name: Model No.2 Chronograph
Lorca.desc: A vintage-inspired hand-wound chronograph with Swiss movement, Lorca's second model.

Anoma.name: A1
Anoma.desc: A rounded-triangle watch inspired by 1950s asymmetric designs, now in a permanent core collection.

Anoma.name: A1 limited editions
Anoma.desc: Small runs of the A1 with special dials or cases, such as Slate stone, Optical op-art and hand-chiselled Prehistoric.
